key_insight: Detonation-sprayed hydroxyapatite coatings improved titanium wear resistance, with the best tribological performance at O₂/C₂H₂ ratios of 3.0 and 3.3.
engineering_relevance: These coatings could extend titanium implant service life by reducing wear in physiological environments.
method: Deposit hydroxyapatite on Grade 2 titanium using O₂/C₂H₂ ratios of 2.6–3.7.
Analyze coating phases by X-ray diffraction.
Evaluate friction and wear under dry conditions and in Ringer’s solution.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports lower wear than uncoated titanium and predominantly hydroxyapatite coatings with partial α-tricalcium phosphate formation, but provides no numerical wear results.
watch_item: Long-term implant durability and biological integration require validation beyond the reported tribological tests.
paper_title: STUDY OF TRIBOLOGICAL PROPERTIES OF BIOCOATINGS BY DETONATION SPRAYING METHOD
